chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: John Coltrane asks where to go next
summary: Coltrane visited him at the Showplace and asked what to do next; Mingus said get out of the rut.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Even John Coltrane copied him.
Yeah. What about Coltrane? Did you know him at all well?

All I know is, he came by one time when I was playing at the Showplace, and he was very (inaudible). Mingus, where do you go from here? What do we do next? I said, what do you mean? Just do another composition.
Yeah.
Stop playing the same thing you've been playing every night. Because he was (inaudible).
Oh, yeah, yeah.
All you do is go to play the Hungarian minor scale.
What did he say?
I didn't tell him that. I told him, all you got to do is get out of the rut he's in, and do something different.
Yeah.
There are so many (inaudible) styles of music to improvise on. I was confused as to why he kept playing that minor scale all the time.
Yeah. Yeah, it's just like writers. I mean, people say, I don't have anything to write about, I don't know what they're talking about.
Well, he asked me that, man. I didn't
even compliment him. Because Charlie Parker would never ask that, he'd just go on and do something else.
Yeah.
Even though it would be based on another tune. John was playing one chord, one point, and he got hung on that. And the time (inaudible).
Yeah, Ted Krusen.
Ted Krusen, well, (inaudible) Ted. He's all right.
Well, you got him to sound better than he ever did before or since.
Yeah. But the things we were doing were definitely John Coltrane.
Yeah.
